title: transit signature verification is best-effort non-fatal: forged articles accepted silently
description:
## What / Why
In crates/transit/src/peering/pipeline.rs, signature verification on ingested articles is explicitly best-effort and non-fatal: a verification failure is logged at WARN level but the article is accepted and written to IPFS and the group log. The comment says 'Signature verification is best-effort (non-fatal).' This means a peer can send an article with an invalid or missing X-Stoa-Sig and it will be stored as if it were legitimate.

## Risk
An adversarial peer (or a misconfigured one) can inject unsigned or forged articles into the group log. These will be replayed to readers and other peers. The security claim that all stored articles carry a valid operator signature is violated at the transit layer.

## Fix
Document this as an intentional design decision if inter-operator trust is not required at the transit layer (i.e., each operator verifies only their own reader-posted articles). If transit verification is required, change the failure path to IngestResult::Rejected. Add a config flag to control behavior.
